signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Weakness
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard displays a critical bilateral divergence with CHF leading gains at +0.992% across 6 pairs while AUD anchors the laggard position at -0.543% across 4 pairs, generating a 1.535% leader-to-laggard spread. AUD/USD trades at 0.6643 while USD/CHF sits at 0.8355, establishing AUD/CHF at 0.5548. RBA at 4.85% vs SNB at 0.00% maintains a nominal +485bp rate differential in AUD's favor, yet the currency cannot draw support while commodity space slides and VIX at 26.4 marks elevated volatility. Technicals reflect structural weakness as AUD/USD holds below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.6863/0.6953/0.7045 in a firm downtrend. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF; risk-off sentiment and G10 relative weakness outweigh the carry advantage. Catalyst: Australia Construction Work Done data at 00:30 UTC. Risk: VIX retracts below 20.0, stabilizing commodity appetite and prompting a sharp carry-seeking bounce.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Geopolitical Stress
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.25, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 158.69/158.04/158.79. 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered BoJ verbal warnings; intervention risk rises on a sustained break above 160. SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23% provides a +269bp OIS carry differential supporting USD, but options markets signal hedging demand with USD/JPY 25d Risk Reversals printing a strong -1.80 put skew. Headlines report a fourth oil tanker exploding near the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining elevated geopolitical stress alongside VIX at 26.4. Cross-asset correlation reveals USD/JPY vs VIX at corr=-0.063 vs norm=+0.271 (z=-2.29σ), showing standard JPY safe-haven relationships remain distorted by carry. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; carry support at 159.25 competes directly with options downside protection and 160.00 intervention friction. Catalyst: BoJ Core CPI figures at 05:00 UTC. Risk: Spot clears 160.00 without official intervention, sparking a squeeze toward multi-decade highs.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs Retail Divergence + ESI Drag
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5485, remaining capped below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5567/0.5623/0.5797 in a confirmed downtrend structure. CFTC data displays NZD LF net short at -23,862 contracts (long% 25.3%), whereas Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers an extreme 91% long / 9% short configuration. This institutional-versus-retail positioning divergence occurs while the NZD Economic Surprise Index stands at -15.4, indicating persistent macroeconomic data misses. Fed 4.00% vs RBNZ 2.75% provides a +125bp nominal rate advantage favoring USD (+125bp cross carry), reinforcing the fundamental backdrop. BEER fair value model flags NZD/USD as cheap at z=-2.03σ (model value 0.5534), though structural flows show no immediate inflection. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; retail long crowding faces downside pressure from institutional shorts and negative macro surprises. Catalyst: US Core PCE Price Index at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Broad USD unwinds force a short-covering rally back toward the SMA20 at 0.5567.
